name: Vincent van Gogh
findings: Within his own canvases, antique brass turns up as a small accent in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 1.9x the archive's rate (from 1228 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, sulphur yellow turns up as the lightest note in 53% of the paintings that hold it, 2.8x the archive's rate (from 1228 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, brazil red turns up as the shadow in 60% of the paintings that hold it, 7.3x the archive's rate (from 1228 paintings here).
Rarely uses smoky black, common in the same museum(s)' other paintings (from 1228 paintings here).
Pairs deep slate-violet with old lavender more than chance would predict (3 of 1228 paintings here).
Pairs cinereous with silver pink more than chance would predict (3 of 1228 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (dark olive brown, seaweed green, lemon meringue) covers 54% of his paintings here.
Keeps 2 distinct palette families here, from dark olive brown, seaweed green to smoky black, dark jungle green.
